3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: Inside the building, I was greeted by Ciara's assistants. They led me to a meeting room where she was waiting inside. She stood and gripped my hand.

5.speaker: Narrator
5.text: Ciara had scheduled a short meeting at the Ministry of Education to discuss the current curriculum taught in schools.

6.speaker: Narrator
6.text: The ministry building was located in the government district right next to the Ministry of Health. It was tall, narrow and wedge-shaped, like a slightly opened book.

7.speaker: Narrator
7.text: Near the front gate, there were many statues of world-renowned scientists and thinkers. The largest, of course, was of Artvin Einstavn, the greatest scientist of all time.

8.speaker: Narrator
8.text: Above the main entrance was the familiar inscription, 'Instreten sis er Anginicar av Gereigna, int olla Almergwolltene, int olla Mexis'. 'Education is the premise of progress, in all societies, in all families.'

12.speaker: Ciara Walda
12.text: “I will cut straight to the chase.”

16.speaker: Ciara Walda
16.text: “Our progressive reform of the Sordland education system is well underway. But there is one sticking point.”

17.speaker: Ciara Walda
17.text: “You've elected not to reform the Sordland education system -- I've already voiced my many objections to that, but I respect your decision. There is, however, one sticking point."

19.speaker: Player
19.text: “I don't see a problem with teaching our children both theories.”

20.speaker: Ciara Walda
20.text: “As it currently stands, schools across Sordland can decide whether to include evolution, creationism or both in their curriculum."

21.speaker: Player
21.text: “I don't agree with teaching our children supernatural nonsense like creationism.”

22.speaker: Player
22.text: “Evolution is the idea that ought to be banned. It's dangerous."

23.speaker: Ciara Walda
23.text: “That's great to hear! It sounds like we are already aligned on the matter.”

24.speaker: Ciara Walda
24.text: “That would be one way to compromise, yes. But does creationism really help open the minds of our children?”

25.speaker: Ciara Walda
25.text: “The way I see it, it promotes the blind acceptance of the world as it is, no facts or verification needed."

26.speaker: Ciara Walda
26.text: "Children should be encouraged to think critically and ask questions. Creationism and other religious teachings hinder that.”

28.speaker: Ciara Walda
28.text: "Children should be encouraged to think critically and ask questions. Creationism and other religious teachings hinder that.”

29.speaker: Player
29.text: “There must be a place for our religion in schools. How else will children learn moral correctness?"

30.speaker: Player
30.text: “Nonsense. Learning about creationism doesn't mean that you are not questioning.”

31.speaker: Player
31.text: “What about this so-called *evolution theory*? Why should children blindly accept that?”

32.speaker: Ciara Walda
32.text: “How does encouraging schools to reject evolution make sense? Do you think learning about evolution makes a person question less?”

33.speaker: Ciara Walda
33.text: “It's the exact opposite. Evolution is a theory that was created by using observational data over the span of many years.”

34.speaker: Ciara Walda
34.text: “I might add that evolution is also most likely going to be proven in the future, as there is empirical evidence.”

35.speaker: Player
35.text: “*Most likely*. You are saying this while it is certain that the word of God is true.”

36.speaker: Ciara Walda
36.text: “Learning about religion does not make everyone morally correct, does it?”

37.speaker: Ciara Walda
37.text: "Are you forgetting the recent religiously motivated terror attacks? Or that according to Nurity, women like myself are second-class citizens?"

39.speaker: Ciara Walda
39.text: “You know what? This is going nowhere.”

40.speaker: Ciara Walda
40.text: “Learning about the history of creationism is fine. That's not the problem. The problem is when you see people call ideas like evolution "dangerous".

41.speaker: Player
41.text: “My evidence is God. You can look anywhere in the beauty of the world and see the evidence.”

42.speaker: Ciara Walda
42.text: “Whereas religion demands we believe in the word of one book, many scientists have worked on countless experiments.”

44.speaker: Ciara Walda
44.text: “That sort of dogmatic thinking is exactly the problem.”

45.speaker: Ciara Walda
45.text: “When you look at these buildings, these cars or planes, the product of human work and technology, do you see God?”

46.speaker: Ciara Walda
46.text: “I see people. I see scientists and researchers. Not God. People made those.”

47.speaker: Ciara Walda
47.text: “Without changing your perspective by learning about new things, how are we going to ever progress?”

48.speaker: Ciara Walda
48.text: “How is that not the same thing? You just said religion brings moral correctness.”

50.speaker: Player
50.text: “Nurity has brought us so far. Why are you denying it all?”

52.speaker: Ciara Walda
52.text: “Your kind of dogmatic thinking is exactly the problem.”

53.speaker: Ciara Walda
53.text: “Without changing your perspective by learning about new things, how are we going to ever progress?”

54.speaker: Ciara Walda
54.text: “Because to change the future, sometimes you need to accept that the past is wrong.”

56.speaker: Player
56.text: “How dare you defy the one true law of the universe? God.”

57.speaker: Ciara Walda
57.text: “The problem is creationism says that it knows *the answer* without any evidence.”

59.speaker: Ciara Walda
59.text: “There is clearly no point in discussing this with you.”

60.speaker: Player
60.text: “How dare you defy the one true law of the universe? God.”

61.speaker: Player
61.text: “How dare you defy the one true law of the universe? God.”

62.speaker: Player
62.text: “You know what I think? Evolution poisons young minds.”

63.speaker: Ciara Walda
63.text: “How can you say that? With what evidence do you say that? Let me guess. None.”

65.speaker: Ciara Walda
65.text: “That's fine. I can live with that.”

66.speaker: Ciara Walda
66.text: “When I look at nature, I see biology. I see chemistry. I don't see a God under my microscope.”

67.speaker: Player
67.text: “Regardless, I don't believe schools need to ban creationism entirely. I don't see the harm in letting students decide for themselves.”

70.speaker: Player
70.text: “You have a point. Perhaps there is no place for creationism in schools.”

72.speaker: Lucian Galade
72.text: “Excuse me. Some urgent business kept me away.”

75.speaker: Player
75.text: “Glad you came. I need to hear some opinions that make sense.”

78.speaker: Player
78.text: “We were just discussing the curriculum. Ciara has made some excellent points.”

79.speaker: Lucian Galade
79.text: “The General Staff had some concerns about the Rumburg border. I already provided you with a report. Nothing else.”

84.speaker: Ciara Walda
84.text: “...It is my conviction that we should require the mandatory teaching of evolution in Sordland's public schools and cut creationism completely out.”

85.speaker: Ciara Walda
85.text: “If we want children from rural areas to have the same opportunities as their urban counterparts, this is the way.”

86.speaker: Ciara Walda
86.text: “Opening students' minds and reducing the role of religion in schools will also lead to more equality between young men and women.”

87.speaker: Lucian Galade
87.text: “Don't bring your pet cause into this, Ms. Walda. You failed your reforms, and now you want to remove belief from schools?”

91.speaker: Ciara Walda
91.text: “Advancing women's rights is more than just a pet cause. Both of you gentlemen must know that."

92.speaker: Ciara Walda
92.text: “Also, we all know why the education reforms failed. Don't we?”

94.speaker: Player
94.text: “Yes, and I am disappointed. I expected more from you.”

95.speaker: Player
95.text: “Your education budget didn't make the cut. Nothing can be done about it.”

96.speaker: Narrator
96.text: Ciara's eyes widened in disbelief and she opened her mouth to say something but she didn't.

97.speaker: Ciara Walda
97.text: “Action and consequence. I told you before.”

100.speaker: Lucian Galade
100.text: “Although I myself believe in evolution, we must be careful not to alienate our rural conservative voter base."

101.speaker: Lucian Galade
101.text: “We owe a lot to their support. Forcing their school districts to teach evolution could irreparably damage our standing with them."

102.speaker: Ciara Walda
102.text: “Every modern nation is reducing or removing creationism in their curriculum. Yet we are supposed to allow schools to promote fundamental -- and, yes, sexist -- ideas from a thousand years back?”

103.speaker: Lucian Galade
103.text: “So is that what we are doing now? Copying what other nations are doing instead of paving our own way?”

104.speaker: Ciara Walda
104.text: “If it works, why not? Look at the analysis. It is clear that the superpowers are doing something right.”

105.speaker: Narrator
105.text: Their voices started to get louder and louder. I held up my hands for silence.

106.speaker: Ciara Walda
106.text: “Should we reinvent the wheel, Mr. Galade? You speak as if we don't import *any* influences from other countries.”

108.speaker: Player
108.text: “We can still allow creationism to be taught alongside evolution. Ciara, you could live with that.”

109.speaker: Ciara Walda
109.text: "Yes, although I won't like it. I still believe schools are no place for religion."

110.speaker: Player
110.text: “Schools should be able to teach creationism exclusively.”

111.speaker: Player
111.text: “Evolution is the way forward. Creationism has no place in the public school curriculum.”

112.speaker: Ciara Walda
112.text: “Thank you! As I said, it's the only way to produce a new generation of thinkers.”

113.speaker: Ciara Walda
113.text: “I can't believe you're ignoring all my arguments. What is the motivation here? To go back to 1739?”

114.speaker: Lucian Galade
114.text: “The motivation is to respect the beliefs of Sordland's heartland, not foist unwanted teachings on them.”

115.speaker: Lucian Galade
115.text: “There are other methods of bringing Sordland forward. Ones that don't sever our ties with an entire voter base."

116.speaker: Lucian Galade
116.text: “I won't like it, either. You'll have to prepare to lose a lot of voters."

117.speaker: Narrator
117.text: Ciara looked me in the eye.

118.speaker: Ciara Walda
118.text: “It is your decision. Don't forget, future generations of Sordish youth are counting on you.”

119.speaker: Player
119.text: “I will make the teaching of evolution mandatory, but schools may promote creationism alongside it if they wish."

120.speaker: Player
120.text: “From now on, creationism shall be banned and only evolution will be taught in schools.”

121.speaker: Player
121.text: "We will stick to the current system. Evolution will not be mandatory, and schools that wish to teach creationism exclusively may do so."

132.speaker: Ciara Walda
132.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Turn04_PSnW_Education_Progressive"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn04_PSnW_Education_Progressive"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Media_SordlandToday_Bias"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Media_SordlandToday_Bias"] == true) == false)

133.speaker: Lucian Galade
133.text: “Unfortunate, but it will have a better outcome than banning creationism altogether.”

135.speaker: Lucian Galade
135.text: “This will certainly help us retain our popularity among conservatives. Also, a less educated populace is more easily managed.”

136.speaker: Lucian Galade
136.text: “As your chief strategist, my job is to advise you on the political landscape and I can guarantee that this won't do us well.”

137.speaker: Ciara Walda
137.text: “I disagree. Rejecting creationism would have been a signal that we were redirecting Sordland toward a scientifically and technologically advanced future.”

138.speaker: Ciara Walda
138.text: “Sometimes there are more important things, Mr. Galade.”

140.speaker: Ciara Walda
140.text: “I can't believe you just said that.”

141.speaker: Narrator
141.text: They turned and looked at each other. Lucian lifted his eyebrow and Ciara held his gaze for a couple of seconds.

148.speaker: Ciara Walda
148.text: "Rural schools often decide in favor of creationism only, which puts students at a disadvantage when it comes to entering university. The effect is especially noticeable among young women."

149.speaker: Ciara Walda
149.text: "My suggestion is to make the teaching of evolution mandatory, and preferably ban creationism altogether."

150.speaker: Ciara Walda
150.text: "It promotes the blind acceptance of the world as it is, no facts or verification needed."

151.speaker: Ciara Walda
151.text: "Your budget cuts may have put the brakes on our plans for education reform but there is one important change that can still be made."

155.speaker: Lucian Galade
155.text: "Ms. Walda, don't bring your pet cause into this. Mr. President, there are other considerations you may not have thought about."
